title: The AI Supply Chain Paradox: When Digital Intelligence Strengthens Resilience but Creates New Systemic Fragilities
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to strengthen supply-chain resilience through improved forecasting, anomaly detection, information processing, resource allocation and disruption response. Recent evidence supports this view, yet the same transformation creates a less examined tension: AI-enabled supply chains increasingly depend on specialised hardware, cloud infrastructure, data, software, foundation models and concentrated technology providers. This essay develops a resilience–fragility paradox in which AI may strengthen resilience at the operational level while simultaneously creating new dependencies at the digital-infrastructure and ecosystem levels. The argument is not that AI inherently makes supply chains fragile. Rather, the resilience contribution of AI should be evaluated together with the dependencies introduced by the infrastructure required to sustain AI-enabled operations. Drawing on recent research on AI-enabled resilience, supply-chain viability, AI infrastructure concentration, third-party dependency and cyber risk, the essay proposes a dual-layer perspective distinguishing operational intelligence from digital dependency. It argues for a shift from AI adoption toward AI dependency management, including dependency mapping, substitutability, interoperability, graceful degradation, human fallback capacity and digital stress testing. The essay concludes with implications for resilient-by-design AI-enabled supply networks and future research.
